name: separation-witness
comment: X-28's WITNESS, and the role the shared spawn point kept putting in the line of fire.
In x25-torso-aim-02 the resolver's nearest target was this client at 2.7 m while the
shooter aimed at the other; combat-observer-b.json's seven-second strafe bought two runs
in three, which is separation by luck rather than by construction.
This walks OUT rather than strafing across: a strafe stays broadside to the shooter's
line, so a few metres of it only moves the witness along the arc the resolver scans. Yaw
90 with sprint leaves the engagement altogether, and then it holds --
a witness still walking during the fire window would make each run's geometry different,
which is the reproducibility this set is for.
It never fires. A third shooter would make every killfeed line ambiguous about who killed
whom, which is the ambiguity check 1 spent three runs on.
X-88: the walk was twenty-two seconds of sprint, roughly 154 m, four times the distance
that put a driver in the water on a neighbouring programme. It is now eight, and the
fourteen seconds removed were handed to the in-range hold rather than to the clock, so
every checkpoint from `firing` onward begins at the same absolute second it always did
and the two clients stay in phase. Eight seconds of sprint still clears the resolver arc,
which is what the paragraph above actually asks for -- the rest was margin nobody had
measured. The grader now fails a run whose observer entered water at all, so a scenario
that drifts back into this cannot report itself as `witness saw nothing`.
